implementation_notes: The standard library is the cache: functools.lru_cache(maxsize=...) turns any hashable-key function into a bounded LRU cache, functools.cache() is its unbounded form, and the wrapper's cache_clear()/cache_info() expose invalidation and hit/miss statistics without extra code. cached_property covers the per-instance derived-field case. The classic structure - hash table plus recency list - collapses into the decorator, so only TTL, weight-based bounds or a shared cross-process store still need a library (cachetools, Redis). Keep the classic hand-written form for caches that must be introspected, resized or partitioned by key family.
pitfalls: The key is built from call arguments using their hash/equality contract: mutable or identity-based objects can miss unexpectedly or change meaning after insertion -> pass stable scalar keys or immutable value objects.
Decorating an instance method keys on self, pinning every instance that was ever passed for as long as the (process-wide) cache lives; use cached_property or an explicit per-instance dict instead.
functools.cache never evicts: unbounded memory growth by design.
Exceptions are not cached, so a failing loader is retried on every call - cache the failure explicitly or accept the retry cost.

variants.name: cachetools TTLCache/LRUCache as an explicit mapping
variants.implementation_notes: cachetools provides the policies functools lacks: TTLCache (per-entry TTL with maxsize), LRUCache, LFUCache and RRCache are plain mutable mappings with a lock parameter for thread safety, and the cached()/cachedmethod() decorators wrap them around functions and methods. Choose it when entries must expire (functools.lru_cache has no TTL), when the bound should be policy-selectable, or when one cache object must be shared, inspected or cleared selectively by several call sites.
pitfalls: TTLCache expires lazily: expired entries stay in the mapping until they are touched, so len() overstates the live set and iteration can yield stale keys.
cachedmethod keys on self, pinning instances for the cache's lifetime unless the cache is cleared per request or keyed by a stable id.
A cachetools cache is not process-shared: under multiple workers each process keeps its own copy, so invalidation only reaches the worker that handled the write.
